title: PATHS: Exploring the relationships between physiological, personal, social, and environmental resources, GPS-based life-space mobility, and frailty – A feasibility study
summary:
Frailty is a complex condition associated with aging that is characterized by a decline in health resources, reduced resilience, and a threat to older adults’ ability to perform daily activities and live independently. The causal relationships contributing to the development and persistence of frailty syndrome are diverse. Resources at various levels (physiological, personal, social, and environmental resources) and their interactions play a decisive role. In particular, the role of older adults’ mobility outside the home (also known as life-space mobility) has been little studied. The project will conduct a feasibility study to enable the scientific investigation of these relationships in a larger study  aiming to gain new insights into the prevention of frailty syndrome. The study uses validated questionnaires (assessments), saliva samples, and measurements of out-of-home mobility using GPS (Global Positioning System) technology over a 30-day period, as well as a paper-based  activity diary. The questionnaires (assessments) and measurement methods used assess the health resources of older adults (70+ years) at various levels as well as their out-of-home mobility. In total two study sessions and the GPS-based assessment of out-of-home mobility with activity diary will be conducted over approximately 6 weeks.  To determine whether the methods used are practical and well-accepted by the participants , a questionnaire assessing feasibility and acceptance is administered, and interviews are conducted with the participants after each study appointment .

To assess and improve the acceptability and clarity of the activity diary, an additional focus group will be held with five participants after the completion of the study appointments.

Study participants will also be asked whether they consent to the collection and storage of a saliva sample for future interdisciplinary research (geriatrics, gerontology, social sciences, biology, computer science). Collected saliva samples will be stored in the biobank of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin and the Berlin Institute of Health (BIH). Participants may also take part in the study without providing a saliva sample.
conditions: Persons with different states of frailty (robust, pre-frail, frail)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The participant's capacity to give consent

- Sufficient vision and hearing to understand the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cognitive impairments / dementia
-    Inability to understand or follow participant instructions

-    Severe psychological or emotional impairments

-    Insufficient understanding of the German language

-    Presence of an acute emergency or acute serious infection

-    Events in the past four weeks that have limited mobility and will significantly alter the participant’s usual mobility outside the home over the next 6 weeks

-    Planned extended vacations (> 10 days) or hospital stays  within the next six weeks (absence from one's place of residence)

- Living in Berlin/Brandenburg
